questions.question: Define globalisation and give three reasons why countries trade with each other.
questions.expected_answer: Globalisation is the process by which the economies, cultures and societies of countries become more closely connected and dependent on each other through trade, investment, technology and the movement of people. Reasons (any three): resources are unevenly distributed (e.g. SA has platinum but imports crude oil); climates differ; skills and technology differ; large-scale production lowers costs; specialisation according to comparative advantage raises total output.

questions.question: A country exports goods worth R95 million and imports goods worth R110 million. Calculate the balance of trade and state whether it is a surplus or deficit. Then, at R18 per dollar, calculate the rand cost of a 500-dollar import.
questions.expected_answer: Balance of trade = 95 - 110 = -15, a deficit of R15 million (imports exceed exports). Cost = 500 × 18 = 9 000 rand.

questions.question: Explain one benefit and one cost of globalisation for South Africa, and name two organisations or agreements involved in trade.
questions.expected_answer: Benefit (any one): larger markets for exports and jobs (e.g. the motor industry), wider consumer choice and lower prices, foreign investment, technology transfer, tourism. Cost (any one): job losses in industries facing cheap imports (e.g. clothing and textiles), exposure to global shocks (2008 crisis, COVID-19), dependence on raw-material exports, profits flowing abroad, rising inequality. Organisations: any two of WTO, IMF, World Bank, SACU, SADC, AfCFTA, BRICS, G20.
